reporting-org.narrative: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

description.narrative: ltpgtAligned to the fragility of the Syrian context and despite the December 2024 political change, emergencies due to natural disasters (earthquake, drought, etc), communal clashes, sectarian conflict, and regional conflict (mainly Lebanon) continue to cause displacement and further vulnerabilities across the IDPs, returnees, and host communities. ltbrgtTo be able to respond at the onset of an emergency and align with the strategy of the allocation under envelope 3, NRC is proposing a rapid response intervention across areas of operation in Syria (Rural Damascus, Damascus, Dar’a, ltugtltbgtAs-Sweidaalt/bgtlt/ugt, Homs, Hama, Aleppo, Al Hassakeh, Raqaa, and Qamishli). The interventions will provide life-saving assistance based on the crisis and needs analysis, and may include, but not limited to, interventions, i.e., Water, Sanitation and Hygiene “WASH”, Shelter NFI provision, and multi-purpose cash assistance. Any response activity will be protection-based to enable highly vulnerable people to meet their immediate survival needs and enhanced protection. The NRC aims to reach 13,189 individuals through this contingency fund. The selection of specific locations is based on emergency needs, which will be well-coordinated with national and sub-national sector/clusters and the SHF. The proposed integration between the different sectors will demonstrate a greater impact on the population, while protection aspects will be mainstreamed throughout all the interventions.ltbrgtThe crisis trend analysis conducted by NRC, combined with the current situation in the country, resulted in various triggers that make mandatory early preparedness and response capacities highly critical. These triggers are marked by the following events:ltbrgt- Sudden displacements and return of population triggered by armed clashes and violent conflicts or premature returns are still a possibility in different parts of Syria, as it has been witnessed in coastal areas and the South of Rural Damascus and across other parts of Syria. ltbrgt- Cholera outbreaks: given the current water scarcity situation and the perspective of having water shortages in many areas of the country until the next rains in Winter, the risk of cholera is expected to be high this year. The wastewater treatment facilities are non-existent in most areas of the country and wastewater is often used for irrigation. This makes the likelihood of cholera and other waterborne diseases very high.ltbrgt- Natural disasters: given the fragile context in Syria, the impact of natural hazards can be very high in different areas of the country. Some potential natural hazards are earthquakes like the one happened in 2023, floods in the NWS or wildfires in the coastal areas, Hama and Homs.ltbrgt- Recent drought faced by Syria due to low rainfall in decades could lead to high level of food insecurity, starvation and potentially famine situation in country cannot be ruled out which will necessitate a response to life saving efforts. ltbrgtEscalation in regional conflict, as witnessed in past in case of Lebanese influx, could result in mass displacement of both Syrian refugees in neighboring countries, or host population (i.e., Palestinians, Iraqis, and other nationalities) to Syria.ltbrgtlt/pgt
